key_insight: SkillScaffold learns when a generated skill will actually help, then injects it selectively so the agent benefits from reusable guidance without forcing unnecessary skills.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to reduce rollout cost and improve stability in agentic RL systems by adapting skill use to the current policy and task difficulty.
method: Reuse outcome-verified trajectories to generate candidate textual skills.
Estimate each skill’s utility via outcome-aware likelihood comparisons instead of extra environment rollouts.
Inject only helpful skills; abstain and run skill-free when no candidate is predicted to help.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and τ²-Bench across both short- and long-horizon tasks, with ablations supporting utility-based selection and abstention.
watch_item: Utility estimation relies on likelihood-based proxies, so performance may depend on how well these scores correlate with real downstream skill benefit under new tasks or policies.
paper_title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
